feature: opt-in safe-stop selection for native FreeDOS save keeps

applied_verification.result: patch applied to an isolated copy containing only its six existing N23 files; all seven patched outputs matched the N24 source hashes

api.vmstate: native save-witness parent VMState schema version 3, minimum version 3; same-binary N24 restore only
api.trigger: one opt-in stop attempt at a matching completed AH=0Dh return only when the v2 save witness is valid and ready; enabling at an already-ready ledger does not synthesize a stop
api.stop_boundary: the native IRET helper records its return CS:IP/SS:SP and requests cpu_stop_current; the main-loop handler records PAUSED only if that request wins, otherwise records a preempted receipt

build.build_result: Build 02 compiled and linked successfully after replacing a target-specific include in common runstate with a registered callback.

qualification.status: bounded N24 native save-safe-stop suite passed; broader preservation qualification owned by root
qualification.native_scope: one native save-observer flow with opt-in safe stop at completed AH=0Dh; BP/hook conflict precedence, pending IRET checkpoint behavior, script/trial/internal-path suppression, and journal failure handling.

limits: Safe stop is disabled by default and applies only to explicit public workspace save-keep runs.
A stop attempt is one-shot. A settled receipt must be persisted and ACKed before reconfiguration; repeated eligible flush before ACK invalidates auxiliary stop control.
A pending stop handoff is not checkpointable. Settled consumed/preempted receipts and policy are preserved in N24 VMState; a restored receipt is not replayed.
The native receipt records the exact returned source location but does not claim guest instruction retirement beyond the IRET boundary.
Preexisting debugger, single-step, breakpoint, active clock-budget, or display-frame stop ownership is preserved and reported as preemption/conflict.
Same-binary N24 restore only; no N23-to-N24 or cross-binary native VMState compatibility claim.
No hosted CI, cross-architecture, DOSBox parity, or default automatic keep claim.
